findings.evidence: Lines 333-336 and 437-443 both reduce to `simp only [... hk, hk']; ring` on the same quadratic expansion.

findings.issue: `trueInvariants_Q2_of_collinear_initialState` (line 330) and `electronMethod_Q2_of_collinear_finalState` (line 425) are two instances of one identity, each expanded inline under `hk`/`hk'`. The identity needs no mass-shell hypothesis: for all `u v z`, `-g (z•u - v) (z•u - v) = z * (-g (u - v) (u - v)) + (1 - z) * (z * g u u - g v v)` (expand: LHS = -(z²a - zS + b), RHS = -za + zS - zb + (1-z)(za - b) with a = g u u, b = g v v, S = g u v + g v u).

For the ISR statements the photon is collinear with `k` (`hcol : e.photon = (1 - z) • e.k`, line 331), so only `g k k = 0` is forced; `hk' : g e.kPrime e.kPrime = 0` is an independent masslessness assumption on the outgoing lepton that nothing in the hypotheses implies.

findings.issue: `mixedMethod.x` is written `-g (k-k') (k-k') / (2 * g p k * (g p (pX - p) / g p k))`; the `g p k` factors cancel wherever `g p k ≠ 0`, so the only effect of keeping them is a junk value at `g p k = 0`, which forces the extra hypothesis `hpk` in `mixedMethod_eq_trueInvariants_of_photon_eq_zero` (line 269). Unlike `sigmaMethod`, whose `y_Σ` has no `p·k` to cancel, nothing here requires the uncancelled form.

summary: The covariant methods and the collinear statements sit at a reasonable level, but two Q² results are the same hypothesis-free algebraic identity proved twice under mass-shell assumptions, the Born-limit group reproves a special case of an unconditional theorem in the same file, and `mixedMethod.x` carries a cancelling `p·k` factor that forces a spurious hypothesis.
